summary: EditClient::list_boards calls the authenticated GET /navigation/boards on hosts started with discovery enabled. The host access module owns workspace and board visibility for both listing and target authorization. PostgreSQL filters and orders the catalog before each 2,000-row limit; the client preserves that order. Item reads and writes remain restricted to the configured target.
evidence: list_visible_boards_in_navigation_order: over real loopback HTTP the Member received Amber, Cedar, Quartz; the Viewer received Ash, Amber, Quartz, Pine. Each response matched the expected ordered board UUID, workspace UUID and name with no extra fields. A missing bearer returned 401; the ordinary single-board host returned 404 for the same Member's list request.

The boundary fixture added 1,999 earlier visible workspaces and 2,000 later boards. The Viewer received exactly Amber, Quartz and the first 1,998 added board tuples. The inactive workspace did not consume a slot; the later closed workspace was outside the workspace limit even though its creator could otherwise read it.

workspace_membership_changes_refresh_list_and_access: the subscribed Member initially got 403 reading and renaming Ash. After a separately committed workspace membership, the same bearer listed Ash, Amber, Cedar, Quartz, Pine and read Ash with the edit hint. GET and PUT for listed non-target Amber returned 404. Demotion preserved the list but removed the edit hint and denied the rename. Removing membership removed Ash and Pine and denied target access again.

Making the subscription table unavailable in the disposable schema returned 503; restoring it let the same session list Amber, Cedar, Quartz again. Closing the remaining open workspace returned an empty list while session resolution still succeeded. Revocation then returned 401 on list. Fresh connections around the denials confirmed the expected role, memberships, four board subscriptions, session account links, and target IDs 42 then 17, both Review/1.

A populated packet 14 private policy and subscriber were migrated on host startup. The subscriber's session saw an empty discovery list but could save and reopen the target directly. Removing its policy denied further board access without invalidating the session.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed all 21 tests, including all seven loopback_board_access cases. All 11 inherited windows_smoke cases passed serially in graphical Windows processes. Workspace formatting and git diff --check passed. The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs; Node runner regressions remain for coordinator verification.

The Member ordering and join/leave results match the coordinator's recorded synthetic reference operation. No new reference or native sidebar run was performed. Opening another board in a window, history/links, inactive recovery, Owner/Guest visibility and cross-installation collation remain open.
